mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 0.5% coincident with a drop in housing starts (HOUST) below a 12-month moving average triggers a negative demand shock, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY < -0.5% AND HOUST < 12-month moving average
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 YoY < -0.5% and HOUST falls below its 12-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4.5% for four consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing corporate profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE remains below 4.5% for four consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) for six consecutive months indicates a broad-based contraction in economic output, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines for six consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both CPIAUCSL (year-over-year inflation) above 2.5% and FEDFUNDS above 2.5% signals a dual shock of high inflation and restrictive monetary policy, which erodes real corporate earnings and triggers negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both CPIAUCSL > 2.5% and FEDFUNDS > 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average, combined with a decline in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1), signals a shift from spending to saving, which depresses demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average AND GDPC1 < 12-month moving average for 3 months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS exceeds its 12-month moving average and GDPC1 is below its 12-month moving average for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 0.5% month-over-month for two consecutive months signals a strong labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate revenues, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS rises by more than 0.5% month-over-month for two consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on positive relationship exists between the level of the housing starts index (HOUST) and S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, such that higher HOUST values predict higher SPX returns within the short horizon.
failure_condition: The correlation between HOUST and S&P 500 5-day forward returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) in out-of-sample tests.
